dedupe_keys.name: agent based model to assess resilience and efficiency of food supply chains netlogo

description: This NetLogo model of a generic food chain network was written by George van Voorn and Geerten Hengeveld and peer reviewed in the CoMSES library in 2020. Stylised producers, traders and consumers exchange crop items, and the model tracks the changing, disaggregated flows between them while representing agent behaviour explicitly. Resilience and efficiency are measured with the ecological concept of ascendency and linked to how far the overall goal, that every consumer meets their food needs, is fulfilled. Different network structures can be combined with different behaviours. It accompanies a paper in PLOS ONE. Version 1.0.0 is free to download from CoMSES under the GPL-3.0 licence and has a DOI. Caveats: the network is generic, not a real supply chain, so real studies need data on actors and flows. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: comparing how network structure and trader behaviour trade off efficiency against resilience to disruption. Related records: DARTS (model-darts-food-system), from overlapping authors, applies a similar approach to global food security shocks.
inputs: Network of producers, traders and consumers and its structure
name: Agent-based model to assess resilience and efficiency of food supply chains (NetLogo)
